name: Radio Group
hint: Pick another option, or use the arrow keys: the dot travels.
description: Radio buttons for one choice out of a few, all visible, each with a line of explanation, on real native radios (one Tab stop, arrow keys, required, form reset). There is one selection dot per group: when the choice changes it travels from the old ring to the new one on a spring, stretching along its direction of travel and settling round, and the new ring tightens around it as it lands. Also exports Radio for markup between options.
intents: choose one option from a short list
pick one setting in a form
radio group for delivery or frequency options
usage: Use for one choice out of a few (two to six) where every option should stay visible and each is explained by a line of text: how often a digest is sent, a shipping speed, a seat type. Pass `options` ([{ value, label, description?, disabled? }]), `label` (rendered as the <legend>), then `value` + `onChange(value, option, event)` (controlled) or `defaultValue`. Inside a <form> set `name` (generated when absent, so the radios still form one group); `required` blocks the submit natively and a form reset returns to `defaultValue`. `bordered` draws the options as hairline rows in one card, like a settings list; `orientation="horizontal"` puts short options in wrapping rows. `readOnly` keeps the choice focusable and announced but fixed. When options need a card each with an icon, price or artwork, use Choice Cards; for two to five one-word options that switch a view, use Segmented Control; for a long list, use Select; for several choices at once, use CheckboxGroup (from Checkbox). Need markup between options? Use children: <RadioGroup label="..."><Radio value="a" label="..." /></RadioGroup>. The ref goes to the <fieldset>, and ref.current.focus() focuses the checked radio, or the first enabled one.

keyboard.does: Moves to the checked option, or the first enabled one when none is checked; the group is one stop.
Moves to the next enabled option and chooses it, wrapping from the last to the first.
Moves to the previous enabled option and chooses it, wrapping from the first to the last.
Moves focus between options without changing the choice.

screenReader: A radiogroup named by `label` (its legend), with `description` and `error` read as the group's description; each radio says its label, its position, whether it is checked, and its own description. With `error` the group is marked invalid; disabled options are announced as unavailable.

dataProps.type: Array<{ value: string; label?: node; description?: node; disabled?: boolean }>
dataProps.description: The choices, in order. A disabled one is skipped by the arrow keys.
Controlled choice. Pass it with onChange; null shows nothing chosen. Leave undefined to let the group keep its own.
Starting choice when uncontrolled; also what a form reset returns to (null: nothing chosen).

dataProps.type: (value: string | null, option: { value: string; label?: node; description?: node; disabled?: boolean } | null, event: Event | null) => void
dataProps.description: (value, option, event) => void, on every change, and with option and event null on a form reset that changes the choice.
The group's <legend>; it names the radiogroup.
A line under the legend, linked with aria-describedby.
Form name shared by the radios; generated with useId when absent.
An error you already have, shown under the group and announced.
Widest the group grows, in px. 0 fills the container.
Radio elements (and any markup between them), used instead of options.
Goes to the <fieldset>; ref.current.focus() focuses the checked radio, else the first enabled one.
Any other attribute (id, aria-*, data-*) goes to the root <fieldset>. className and style are merged with the component's own.

exports.description: One option inside a RadioGroup, for callers who need markup between options. It reads the group (name, selection, size, disabled) through context; outside a group it renders nothing and warns once in development.

props.description: The value this option submits and reports.
Visible label; it names the radio.
This option cannot be chosen and is skipped by the arrow keys.

example:
<RadioGroup
  label="Delivery"
  name="delivery"
  options={[
    { value: "standard", label: "Standard", description: "3 to 5 working days." },
    { value: "express", label: "Express", description: "Next working day if ordered by 2pm." },
    { value: "pickup", label: "Collect in store", description: "Ready in two hours.", disabled: !storeOpen },
  ]}
  value={delivery}
  onChange={(value) => setDelivery(value)}
  required
/>
